list: **Forgetting the inner derivative.** $\dfrac{d}{dx}\sin(2x) = 2\cos(2x)$, not $\cos(2x)$. This is the most common chain-rule error by far.
**Confusing $\sin^2 x$ with $\sin(x^2)$.** $\sin^2 x = (\sin x)^2$ has derivative $2\sin x\cos x$. $\sin(x^2)$ has derivative $2x\cos(x^2)$.
**Changing the inside of the outer function.** In $\dfrac{d}{dx}\sin(x^2) = \cos(x^2)\cdot 2x$, the cosine still contains $x^2$. Only the multiplier outside is the inner derivative.
**Stopping one layer early.** In a three-layer chain like $\sec(\tan\sqrt{x})$ there are three factors to multiply, one per layer.

related.intro: Many definite integrals are solved by spotting a chain-rule pattern in reverse, so the two techniques are worth learning back to back.
